items.snippet: SK hynix Inc., the world’s largest supplier of HBM memory, today filed to list i...
items.raw_snippet: SK hynix Inc., the world’s largest supplier of HBM memory, today filed to list its shares on the Nasdaq stock exchange. SK hynix produces more than half of the world’s HBM memory, the fast, pricey RAM that artificial intelligence chips use to store data. As a result, data can move more quickly between an HBM device and the processor to which it’s attached. The technology is particularly useful for AI models because they move data between the host processor’s logic circuits and memory more often than most other applications. SK hynix’s leadership position in the HBM market can be partly credited to its portfolio of thermal management technologies. HBM modules generate significantly more heat than a standard DRAM chip, which can cause malfunctions in the graphics card to which they’re attached. As the parent company of SiliconANGLE, theCUBE Network, theCUBE Research, CUBE365, theCUBE AI and theCUBE SuperStudios — with flagship locations in Silicon Valley and the New York Stock Exchange — SiliconANGLE Media operates at the intersection of media, technology and AI.

items.title: AI Capital Strategy: IPOs, CapEx and the Race to Fund Compute
items.snippet: HomeBlogAI Capital Strategy: IPOs, CapEx and the Race to Fund Compute. AI Capita...
items.raw_snippet: HomeBlogAI Capital Strategy: IPOs, CapEx and the Race to Fund Compute. AI Capital Strategy: IPOs, CapEx and the Race to Fund Compute. Explore how AI companies are using IPOs, CapEx, cloud contracts, private capital and energy deals to fund the compute infrastructure behind frontier AI. **AI capital strategy** is the way frontier AI companies fund the compute infrastructure needed to train and run advanced models. It includes IPOs, CapEx, debt, cloud contracts, GPU supply agreements, data centers, power procurement and private infrastructure financing. The biggest AI companies are now competing for physical compute, massive GPU clusters, multi-gigawatt data centers, secure power grids, and the long-term capital required to finance them all. In this deep dive, we explore how AI has transitioned from an asset-light software business into a heavy-industry capital race, why CapEx is the new competitive moat, and what this structural shift means for enterprise IT, investors, and the global cloud ecosystem.

items.title: AI Operating Models for Private Equity | Beyond AI Pilots
items.snippet: AI Operating Models for Private Equity. Most software companies are not short of...
items.raw_snippet: AI Operating Models for Private Equity. Most software companies are not short of AI ideas and already have working use cases or copilots in engineering, chatbots in support, automation experiments in operations, AI features on the product roadmap and pilots scattered across functions. What remains unresolved is far more consequential: why this activity is not translating into sustained, portfolio-level value. For PE-backed software companies, fragmented AI adoption is not a technology issue. AI creates enterprise value only when it moves from pilots to operating model: governed workflows, reusable patterns, clear ownership, secure architecture, measurable adoption and execution at scale. That is the new mandate for PE-backed software businesses. The better question now is: what operating model will allow us to scale AI safely, repeatedly and profitably? For software companies, the delivery lifecycle is one of the most immediate and measurable areas for AI impact. For PE-backed software companies, the AI CoE should function as an AI value office.

items.raw_snippet: ## What is xAI's stock symbol? Since it is not publicly listed, there is no xAI stock symbol or xAI ticker symbol assigned for xAI. Private companies typically reserve a stock symbol up to two years prior to an IPO, and disclose this when they file a Form S-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission when they start the IPO process. ## How can I sell xAI stock? xAI stock does not trade publicly on Nasdaq or NYSE because it is still a private company. xAI stock might be available for purchase in the secondary markets, but xAI stock is not available for purchase by the general public, and can not be purchased through traditional brokerage accounts. ## How can I buy xAI stock? Accredited investors can purchase shares in private companies like xAI. Because xAI is privately held, its stock is not available for purchase through public stock exchanges like the NYSE or Nasdaq.

items.title: The Impact of Research Funding on AI Research Performance: A Resource–Structure–Performance (F-S-P) Perspective on Collaboration and Topic Diversity
items.snippet: This implies that funding structurally increases the entropy of the research eco...
items.raw_snippet: This implies that funding structurally increases the entropy of the research ecosystem, thereby enhancing the potential for recombination innovation as proposed by [[27](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-8954/14/7/736#B27-systems-14-00736)]. As a general-purpose technology whose value is realized through recombination with heterogeneous knowledge domains spanning biomedicine, engineering, and social science [[2](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-8954/14/7/736#B2-systems-14-00736)], AI innovation is fundamentally sensitive to the structural conditions—collaborative openness, knowledge diversity, and institutional flexibility—that national funding environments either enable or constrain. We therefore treat funding as the exogenous resource condition (F), corresponding to the slack resources of resource dependence theory [[14](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-8954/14/7/736#B14-systems-14-00736)]; the knowledge and collaboration architecture of the research ecosystem—topic diversity and network structure—as the structural layer (S), which we interpret as the observable trace of the ecosystem’s absorptive and recombinant capability rather than as mere static structure; and academic impact and social diffusion as performance (P). items.snippet: **Summary:** *Inorganic growth through M&A can help tech companies scale revenue...
items.raw_snippet: **Summary:** *Inorganic growth through M&A can help tech companies scale revenue, capabilities, and penetrate the market faster than organic growth alone. For venture-backed (VC) companies targeting a private equity (PE) exit in three to five years, a disciplined acquisition and integration strategy can strengthen valuation, support expansion into adjacent markets, and demonstrate the operational maturity PE investors value.*. By executing a disciplined M&A strategy, technology companies can accelerate growth, expand their customer base, and increase valuation potential far faster than they could through internal resources alone. In the tech industry, where product life cycles are short and competition is fierce, the speed of inorganic growth offers a distinct advantage. Rather than spending time developing a new software module or struggling to penetrate a new geographic market, companies can acquire a smaller competitor or an adjacent technology firm to achieve those goals within months. Regardless of the exact structure, inorganic growth demands robust due diligence, strategic financial and tax planning, and flawless execution to ensure the investment yields the anticipated value.

Orange Appoints Usman Javaid as Chief AI Officer to Drive Artificial Intelligence Transformation  Image Credit: Orange. Orange announced the appointment of Usman Javaid as the Group's Chief AI Officer, effective from 1 September 2026. Reporting directly to Bruno Zerbib, the Group's Chief Technology & Innovation Officer, Usman Javaid will be responsible for accelerating and scaling up Orange's AI initiatives, building on the strong technological foundations already in place. In particular, he will aim to embed AI and agentic AI at the heart of Orange's operations, across networks, customer relations, operations and services for businesses. With its Trust the future strategy, presented in February 2026, Orange has made artificial intelligence a major driver of value creation, serving quality of service, operational excellence, customer experience and the development of new growth opportunities.

items.title: AI-powered BI with Snowflake and Amazon Quick | Artificial Intelligence
items.snippet: # AI-powered BI with Snowflake and Amazon Quick. A *semantic view* is a Snowflak...
items.raw_snippet: # AI-powered BI with Snowflake and Amazon Quick. A *semantic view* is a Snowflake schema object that attaches business definitions (table, relationships, metrics, and dimensions) directly to your data. You can use semantic views in Cortex Analyst and query these views in a `SELECT` statement. In this post, you will learn how to build an end-to-end integration between Snowflake semantic views and Amazon Quick. You start by loading movie review data from Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) into Snowflake, define a semantic view in SQL to add business meaning, explore it with natural-language queries through Cortex Analyst, and then generate an Amazon Quick dataset and dashboard. End-to-end architecture: data flows from Amazon S3 into Snowflake, where a semantic view feeds Cortex Analyst and Amazon Quick Sight. Figure 1: End-to-end architecture—data flows from Amazon S3 into Snowflake, where a semantic view governs business definitions, enabling both Cortex Analyst natural-language queries and Amazon Quick Sight dashboards.
